## The claim

The causal compound-heterozygous pair is the BUB1B stop_gained allele (ClinVar pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1) together with the BUB1B missense allele absent from gnomAD, in trans.

**Prediction if true.** A submission whose rank-1 row holds exactly these two alleles returns full_match_rank = 1, rank_points = 100 and f_max = 1.0 from the challenge scorer.

**What would refute it.** The scorer returns no full match for that row. A partial match (partial_match_rank = 1) would mean exactly one of the two alleles is causal and the other is not; no match at all would mean neither is.

| # | Direction | Strength | Kind | Observation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 19 | supports | 0.60 | measurement | The pair is the only candidate biallelic set the genome-wide coding scan leaves standing under the three conditions (biallelic on PASS calls, a ClinVar pathogenic allele, phenotype rank 30 or better): one gene of 65, BUB1B, with these two alleles and no third. | `methodology/070` |
| 20 | supports | 0.60 | annotation | The stop_gained allele is classified pathogenic/likely pathogenic by multiple ClinVar submitters with no conflicts, condition Mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 1; it truncates BUBR1 in exon 17 of 23, upstream of the C-terminal kinase domain (gnomAD genomes 3.3e-5, exomes 7.9e-5, no homozygote). | `ClinVar:VCV000533901` |
| 21 | supports | 0.50 | annotation | The missense allele is absent from gnomAD v4 genomes and exomes, lies in the last exon inside the C-terminal kinase domain (CDD cd14029), and is called likely pathogenic by AlphaMissense (0.92) with CADD 24.5; SpliceAI predicts no splice effect for it, and none for the two rare intronic BUB1B alleles that would be its only in-callset alternatives. | `methodology/074` |
| 22 | supports | 0.50 | literature | Hanks et al. 2004 established biallelic BUB1B mutations as the cause of MVA with cancer predisposition (Wilms tumour, rhabdomyosarcoma); the reported genotypes combine a truncating allele with a missense allele that leaves residual BubR1, the same shape as this pair - complete loss of BUB1B is embryonic lethal. | `PMID:15475955` |
| 23 | supports | 0.30 | literature | Suijkerbuijk et al. 2010 showed MVA patient cells carry strongly reduced BUBR1 protein and a weakened spindle assembly checkpoint, with missense alleles acting as hypomorphs - consistent with a kinase-domain missense partnering a null allele. | `PMID:20516114` |
| 24 | supports | 0.30 | literature | Rhabdomyosarcoma, the proband's presenting tumour, is a reported malignancy of BUB1B-related MVA (premature chromatid separation syndrome), matching the phenotype prior that favours BUB1B over CEP57. | `PMID:31184400` |
| 25 | neutral | 0.00 | absence | Phase is not established: the two alleles are 9 exons apart, far beyond the read-backed phasing reach, and no parental samples exist; two heterozygous calls are equally consistent with cis. The trans claim rests on the recessive model and on the absence of any other BUB1B candidate, and is what the oracle will test. | `methodology/074` |
| 26 | neutral | 0.00 | absence | Bulk blood WGS shows no allele-balance or depth signature of mosaic aneuploidy on any autosome; a bulk sample cannot detect an aneuploid fraction below roughly 10-15 percent, so this neither supports nor refutes the diagnosis. | `methodology/037` |
| 29 | neutral | 0.00 | annotation | Correction to row 25: the two alleles lie in exons 17 and 23 of the 23-exon MANE transcript (VEP), six exons apart, not nine; the phasing conclusion is unchanged because the distance is tens of kilobases either way. | `methodology/075` |
